Context switching is a proven productivity killer, but so it long waits not doing something else while a long running process completes.

There was a person in the comments who got pissy about "making fun of OCD", but really this is a form of OCD. I've seen anti-anxiety drugs obliterate the obsessive desire for efficiency in every daily action, and OCD is classified as an anxiety disorder.

I am actually fighting against this right now in my life.

Over optimization takes too mych energy and deprives you of part of the fun that comes from relaxing and part of those dead timeframes in which you can get bored and that father a great bunch of brilliant ideas.
It only makes sense. While I wait for things to cook/microwave I'm usually cleaning the kitchen. While I wait for the shower to warm up I clean the bathroom.

The more time I have on my hands, the more I do this. I never would have thought there was a clinical reason for my behavior. I have a designated pocket for anything I'll have to carry, based on frequency of use and if I have to use a certain hand with it. I have routines for practically everything I do. I just ingrained a new behavior two days ago. I like to take my keys with me when I go out on the back porch in case the door locks behind me, but I often forget to either A) lock the back door when I come in or B) put my keys back where they go after coming inside. Now when I come in, I know that I have to do something to make my routine more efficient, and either one triggers the other. They also pair up with going to grab a drink, since doing both of these prompts me to look toward my next move. I like it because it saves time, but I can surely see that I'm slowly weaving my own web of repetitious hell. Someone who was seriously compulsive about this could ruin their day by fastening a button wrong or taking an extra step before putting their pants on sort of stuff. Right now if I mess up I shrug and chalk it up to remembering to do it right the next time.

Hi everyone!

I've started a new subverse, LifeAdvice. In the past, forums have often split advice into multiple subforums (relationships, work, etc). I've seen this result in a lot of drama in the relationship subs, and some apathy in other subs - as well as only attracting "specialized" posters, rather than a variety of opinions.

The goal is for LifeAdvice to become a place for solid, direct, honest advice for people who need it - whether it be about people, careers, education, general living, whatever.
